issues: No integrity problems: the SMILES-keyed feature cache is label-free and deterministic; mixup uses only training rows and labels.
MLPRegressor trained on soft mixup targets gives unbounded scores, which is harmless because the output is rank-averaged and AUROC only uses order.
Recomputed z = (0.0926-0.1299)/(0.0049*sqrt(2)) ≈ -5.38, which matches the harness's -5.371; the candidate is much worse, so reject is correct.
The diff mixes several changes (mixup, regressor instead of classifier, 3 nets instead of 5, max_iter 200 to 100), so the regression can't be traced to one cause.
